name: PageHeader
intent: The top of a page's content: where it sits (breadcrumb), what it is (title, badge, and an optional icon) and the page actions. Below the AppHeader.
usage: Put one PageHeader at the top of each page, under the AppHeader. It is one component: breadcrumbs are the page's parents, all links, starting with Home and then its side-nav section; the header closes the trail with the title as the current crumb, so it always reads Home › section › this page (like Home › Accounts › Northwind Traders). Then the title row with an optional badge, and an icon before the title only when you pass one (none by default), and the page actions on the end. actions are kit Buttons, size sm, with the one strong brand Button last; moreActions puts less-used actions in a More menu before them. sticky is the compact bar for when the page scrolls: one line whose trail ends in the page title, with a raised shadow unless shadow is false. See contracts/pageheader.json for the full contract. On a phone-width header, under 640px of its own width, the title row takes the full width and the actions move onto their own row under it, starting at the start edge; the compact sticky bar stays one 52px line, keeping only the page name in its trail, shortened with an ellipsis when it runs long. The bar adds no side padding of its own: the page inset comes from the layout class around it (contracts/layout.json), so the title lines up with the Sections under it. The bar is the top of the page, so it sits flush against the frame's bar with no page inset above it; the pattern holding it (AppShell, RecordPage) takes care of that.

title.note: The page name. It is the page's h1. PageHeader writes it in title case, so pass the copy either way.

breadcrumbs.itemShape: { label: string; href?: string; onClick?: () => void }
breadcrumbs.note: The parents of this page, all links: Home first, then the side-nav section, then any parent record. PageHeader adds the title as the last, current crumb, so the trail always reads Home › section › this page. On the section's own page, like the Accounts list, the title is the section itself, so pass only Home and the trail reads Home › Accounts.

icon.note: Optional. Leave it out by default: the title stands on its own. Pass a Material Symbols name, like folder_open, only when the page wants an icon before the title; the kit Icon draws it at size lg in the brand color.

badge.note: A status after the title, like Draft. A kit Badge.

actions.note: Kit Buttons, size sm: subtle first, one strong brand Button last. At most five visible actions including More.

moreActions.itemShape: { id: string; label: string; icon?: string; danger?: boolean } | { divider: true }
moreActions.note: Adds a More menu (kit Dropdown, minimal and unbordered) before the actions, for less-used ones. Delete goes last, as danger. Give each one its icon, so the menu reads at a glance.

sticky.note: Compact 52px bar that sticks to the top of the scroll area: the trail ends in the title, no title row. The bar runs the full width of the page, bleeding back out through the page inset and paying it back as padding, so its line reaches both edges and nothing scrolls past it in the gutters while the title stays lined up with the Sections.

shadow.note: With sticky, a subtle line and a shadow that falls downward only, so the full-width bar does not read as a floating card.

useWhen: The top of every page: record pages, lists, settings.
A page that scrolls: switch to sticky once the title scrolls away.
Every screen in an AppShell: pass Home and the side-nav section as breadcrumbs, and any parent record between them and the page.
doNot: Do not invent ContentHeader, PageTitle, TitleBar or a local heading row.
Do not put the app's logo, search or user in it. That is the AppHeader.
Do not put more than one strong brand Button in actions, or more than five visible actions.
Do not give it side padding to inset the page. Wrap the page in .layout-content, which owns that inset.
Do not leave Home out of breadcrumbs, and do not pass the page title as a crumb yourself. PageHeader adds it as the current crumb.
Do not repeat the section as a crumb on the section's own page, like Home › Accounts › Accounts. Pass only Home there.
a11y: A header with the page's h1. In sticky the h1 stays, hidden, and the trail marks the title as the current page.
The breadcrumb is the kit Breadcrumb (a nav named Breadcrumb). More is a kit Dropdown.
The icon is decorative; the title names the page.
The last crumb is the page title, marked aria-current page and not a link.
snippet:
<PageHeader
  breadcrumbs={[{ label: "Home", href: "/" }, { label: "Billing", href: "/billing" }, { label: "Invoices", href: "/invoices" }]}
  title="INV-1042"
  badge="Draft"
  moreActions={moreActions}
  actions={<>
    <Button size="sm">Send</Button>
    <Button size="sm" emphasis="strong" intent="brand">Approve</Button>
  </>}
/>
